helpers.role: Independent oracles: gc.prt readers, Bio.Seq.translate wrappers, index re-extraction, coordinate mapping, and a second six-frame ORF finder written from the definition. Imported as `from orf_oracle import ...` — never `from conftest import ...`, so this round's tests do not collide with gx/, gx/coords/ or gx/crispr/ in one process.

pytest fixtures only: the pinned full-length inputs, the rCRS SeqRecord and its 13 CDS Annotations as the app parses them, and the two subject entry points (find_orfs, the translate edit operation with its warnings captured).

tests.oracle: gx/corpus/ncbi/gc.prt read as text, cross-checked by re-rendering Biopython's tables 1/2/11 back into its ncbieaa/sncbieaa strings; plus an index-derived ORF set over NG_007400.1 for the start-codon requirement.
Bio.Seq.translate on each frame's substring, re-extraction by index from the pinned bases, and orf_oracle.find_orfs_oracle — a second six-frame finder written from gc.prt, not from the subject.

The BiopythonWarning('Partial codon') Bio.Seq.translate raises on a re-extracted interval, and the ORF model's own field list; the inputs are the real MT-ND4 and MT-CYTB coding spans NCBI marks /transl_except=(...,aa:TERM).

The subject's own answer for the reference spelling of the same molecule (pinned against an independent finder by OR-7), plus backend.sequence_text.normalize_template — the app's own definition of what layout is.
The subject's answer for the unrotated pUC19 record. A rotation is the identity on a circular molecule, so no second finder is needed; OR-7 has already pinned the unrotated answer independently.
The 13 /translation qualifiers of NC_012920.1 — recorded literals from NCBI — and gc.prt's tables 1 and 2 for which codons the two read differently.
Bio.Seq.translate on the same bytes, and the BiopythonWarning it raises, captured in-process and compared against what the subject's own result message says.
